title: Proper act of justifying faith is assent; notitia denied as faith act (Bellarmine)
source_text: XXIV. Jam autem, si quis quaerat de fidei salvificae & justificantis actibus, qui & quales illi sunt, in eo consentiunt Doctores omnes Ecclesiae Romanae proprium fidei justificantis actum consistere in assensu quem Fideles adhibent iis omnibus quae Deus revelavit per Verbum suum Ecclesiae traditum, & propter divinam authoritatem & testimonium. Negant vero notitiam esse fidei actum, & fidem esse notitiam, scientiam, seu intelligentiam. Imo pertendit Bellarminus fidem in contrario scientiae, & melius per ignorantiam quam per notitiam definiri. Lib. 1. de Justif. cap. 7. sub finem.
pass_a_gloss: Now if someone asks about the acts of saving and justifying faith, which and of what kind they are, all the doctors of the Roman Church agree that the proper act of justifying faith consists in the assent the faithful give to all that God has revealed through his Word handed down to the Church, and on account of the divine authority and testimony. But they deny that notitia is an act of faith, and that faith is notitia, knowledge, or understanding. Indeed Bellarmine maintains that faith is contrary to knowledge, and is better defined through ignorance than through notitia (De Justif. 1.7 near the end).
pass_b_english: Rome unanimously locates justifying faith proper act in assent to everything God revealed in the Word delivered to the Church, because of divine authority and testimony.

They deny that notitia (acquaintance, knowledge, or understanding) is faith act; Bellarmine even says faith stands against scientia and is better defined by ignorance than by notitia (De Justif. 1.7).
